item.subject: science
item.stem:
The teacher writes one answer on the board: "six". Arjun must invent a curious situation and a scientific question that this answer could fit. Ideas mentioned include germinating seeds, magnets pulling pins, and evaporating puddles.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.A: He imagines six seeds germinating at different rates and asks which conditions make germination faster.
options.B: He invents a situation with six pins and a magnet and asks how the number of pins attracted can be six.
options.C: He asks, "Why do puddles evaporate?" without checking whether "six" answers that question.
options.D: He says a scientific question is valid only when its answer is already known, so inventing a situation is not allowed.
